headline: Toronto's year has two peaks: the playoff run and a summer of Carnival red.
summary: Raptors interest works like a switch. It flips on with the first playoff series and stays high through any run. This season starts with a strong hook: Kawhi Leonard back in the city that won the 2019 title, beside All-Star Scottie Barnes. Treat "We The North" as a year-round civic identity, not a game-day one.

insights.title: Kawhi's homecoming raises the October-November ceiling
insights.detail: The Leonard trade from the Clippers puts a 2019 champion back in Toronto, which should lift preseason and early-season interest above what a 46-win team normally gets. The Raptors have no opening-night or Christmas Day game, so the first home Cup night, Oct 30 against Brooklyn, is the early focal point.
insights.implication: Have a Kawhi-and-Barnes two-generation capsule ready for the first home weeks. Handle the 2019 champion story through licensed, league-cleared channels.

insights.title: Summer wears Raptors red without the Raptors
insights.detail: In July and early August, Raptors gear shows up in Canada Day crowds and at Toronto Caribbean Carnival weekend, with the Grand Parade on the Ontario Simcoe Day long weekend. The Raptors don't own this festival summer, but they can join it. Fandom here sits inside diaspora and civic identity, so engagement stays high with no games.
insights.implication: Use summer for community-led drops that have nothing to do with games: carnival-adjacent colorways and civic product for Canada Day. Don't wait for October.

insights.title: In the playoffs, Toronto takes to the street
insights.detail: Jurassic Park, on Maple Leaf Square outside Scotiabank Arena, and watch parties across the GTA turn every home playoff game into a public gathering. Last season ended in a 4-3 first-round loss to Cleveland, so the appetite is primed.
insights.implication: In March and April, stock playoff tees, hoodies and a Jurassic Park-ready outerwear piece, with capacity to reorder mid-series.

insights.title: Boxing Day, not Christmas, is the gifting peak
insights.detail: Toronto shops on Boxing Day (Dec 26) and through the Canadian holiday season in December. The Raptors have no Christmas Day game. Jersey and hoodie sales spike in the days before and after.
insights.implication: Time holiday product and Boxing Day promotions to the Canadian retail calendar, not the U.S. Christmas Day game slate.

insights.title: Cold months open the door for outerwear
insights.detail: From November to March Toronto is cold and damp, and the Raptors' mid-winter stretch (Family Day, Black History Month, March Break) overlaps with the Leafs' season. Fans dress for the walk to Union Station and the streetcar.
insights.implication: Lead with warm layers, shell jackets and toques that carry the Raptors identity and work outside the arena.

insights.title: Two other pro calendars compete for attention
insights.detail: The Blue Jays can dominate October when they go deep. The Leafs hold the hockey core from October to April, and TFC and the Argos fill the summer. Raptors fans are younger, more diasporic and more street-level than the Leafs' corporate base.
insights.implication: Don't overweight the Leafs-dominated Bay Street crowd. Target Scarborough, Brampton, Mississauga and Regent Park.

productHooks: Kawhi and Barnes homecoming capsule: tees, hoodies and a jersey for the first home Cup night on Oct 30, tied to the 2019 and 2026 stories.
Jurassic Park outerwear: a waterproof shell and toque set in Raptors red, black and silver, made for cold, wet playoff watch parties.
Summer civic drop: a Canada Day and Carnival weekend release with local Caribbean-Canadian designers, outside the NBA calendar.
Boxing Day gift set: jersey-and-hoodie bundles timed to the Canadian retail peak, not to Christmas Day.
City Edition debut kit tied to a Toronto story, pending the league's reveal and a licensed local-artist partner.
watchouts: Carnival and Caribbean imagery belongs to its community. Partner with, credit and pay mas bands and designers, and never use costume imagery as decoration.
Drake, OVO and any 2019 championship footage or marks need explicit licensing.
Canadian national symbols (flag, maple leaf, Royal and government marks) carry use restrictions. Check before using them.
Kawhi Leonard is 35, and the trade left long-dated unprotected picks. Product tied to one player carries health and sentiment risk, so keep the capsule team-first.
